perindopril/valsartan combination therapy has greater beneficial effects than either monotherapy regarding regression of LVH and improvement of aortic arterial stiffness, as assessed by baPWV, in a selected group (patients with LVH and non-dipping pattern) of essential hypertensive subjects.

perindopril-valsartan combination therapy is more effective than either monotherapy for improving the regression of left ventricular hypertropy, reduction of BNP levels and improvement of arterial stiffness.
valsartan and/or perindopril therapy is effective to improve LVH and aortic stiffness in essential hypertensive patients.

the effects of valsartan, perindoprial combination therapy in patients with LVH.
the effects of valsartan combined with perindopril in patients with essential hypertensive and LVH.

the combination of an ACEI and an ARB is a useful and effective therapeutic option for patients with LVH.

combination therapy is more effective for the treatment of hypertension than monotherapy, but it is not always more effective than monotherapy in all patients with hypertension, especially those who do not respond to monotherapy.
the combination therapy with valsartan and a perindopril is a useful and beneficial strategy for the management of essential hypertension in patients with LVH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perindopril-valsartan combination is more effective for the improvement of LVH and aortic stiffness than either monotherapy in essential hypertensive patients.
combination therapy of valsartan with perindopril may be useful for hypertensive patients with high risk of LVH and aortic stiffness.
the addition of perindopril, an ACEI, to valsartan, an ARB, may be beneficial for the treatment of essential hypertension in patients with LVH, particularly in those with non-dipping patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
valsartan and ACEI combination therapy is a promising treatment for essential hypertension with LVH.
the combination therapy of valsartan with perindopril is more efficacious than either monotherapy alone in reducing LVMI, BNP, and baPWV in patients with hypertension and LVH.
